title: Construction Managers
description: Plan, direct, or coordinate, usually through subordinate supervisory personnel, activities concerned with the construction and maintenance of structures, facilities, and systems. Participate in the conceptual development of a construction project and oversee its organization, scheduling, budgeting, and implementation. Includes managers in specialized construction fields, such as carpentry or plumbing.

tasks.text: Direct and supervise construction or related workers.
Plan, organize, or direct activities concerned with the construction or maintenance of structures, facilities, or systems.
Contract or oversee craft work, such as painting or plumbing.
Implement new or modified plans in response to delays, bad weather, or construction site emergencies.
Develop construction budgets to compare green and non-green construction alternatives, in terms of short-term costs, long-term costs, or environmental impacts.
Prepare and submit budget estimates, progress reports, or cost tracking reports.
Prepare contracts or negotiate revisions to contractual agreements with architects, consultants, clients, suppliers, or subcontractors.
Apply for and obtain all necessary permits or licenses.
Develop or implement quality control programs.
Determine labor requirements for dispatching workers to construction sites.
Develop or implement environmental protection programs.
Study job specifications to determine appropriate construction methods.
Investigate damage, accidents, or delays at construction sites to ensure that proper construction procedures are being followed.
Requisition supplies or materials to complete construction projects.
Direct acquisition of land for construction projects.
Inspect or review projects to monitor compliance with building and safety codes or other regulations.
Plan, schedule, or coordinate construction project activities to meet deadlines.
Confer with supervisory personnel, owners, contractors, or design professionals to discuss and resolve matters, such as work procedures, complaints, or construction problems.
Interpret and explain plans and contract terms to representatives of the owner or developer, including administrative staff, workers, or clients.

Perform, or contract others to perform, pre-building assessments, such as conceptual cost estimating, rough order of magnitude estimating, feasibility, or energy efficiency, environmental, and sustainability assessments.
Evaluate construction methods and determine cost-effectiveness of plans, using computer models.
Inspect or review projects to monitor compliance with environmental regulations.

Secure third-party verification from sources, such as Leadership in Energy Efficient Design (LEED), to ensure responsible design and building activities or to achieve favorable LEED ratings for building projects.
Implement training programs on environmentally responsible building topics to update employee skills and knowledge.
Apply green building strategies to reduce energy costs or minimize carbon output or other sources of harm to the environment.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Management of Financial Resources
skills.def: Determining how money will be spent to get the work done, and accounting for these expenditures.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Management of Material Resources
skills.def: Obtaining and seeing to the appropriate use of equipment, facilities, and materials needed to do certain work.

skills.name: Quality Control Analysis
skills.def: Conducting tests and inspections of products, services, or processes to evaluate quality or performance.

skills.name: Project management software
skills.def: Software to plan, organize, staff, or control the completion of a product or set of tasks. Examples: CBS ProLog Manager, HCSS HeavyBid, HCSS HeavyJob, Microsoft Project.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: ArenaSoft Estimating, Jobber Computer Plus, Procore software.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: Email software, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.
